docs.canvasSeats.component: One board, several pairs of eyes — the shape a live table has, standing in one page.
The truth is a SINGLE tree. Every screen is handed a PROJECTION of it: the same board, minus the
subtrees those eyes are denied, plus a camera turned so that seat's edge is the near one. Nothing
downstream knows who is watching — the renderer draws an ordinary board, and the only per-viewer
decision was made once, before mounting.
const truth = board()                       // one tree, shown to nobody directly
mount(pane, project(truth, seat))         // …and one projection each
That is the canon taken literally: the view is LOCAL, so privacy is a fact of the tree and never
of the renderer. A seat is not given a flag to draw differently — it is given a different tree.
Which is why the projection has to be a COPY: two seats cutting into one board would eat each
other's view, and then the truth itself.
Hands are not private here: every hand is in every picture, and what differs between seats is
which SIDE of its cards they are shown — the `others` axis of facing. A finger writes the TRUTH,
never the view, so a move made on one screen is a move every screen sees.
docs.canvasSeats.table: Two, three or four screens on one desk, LIVE. Drag a card on any screen and it changes owner in the board everyone shares, then every screen is shown again — one truth, several projections, exactly the shape a table over a network has. Each hand carries a facing rule: with `back` a seat reads its own cards and everyone else sees a row of backs, and a card moved into the open middle turns face-up for the whole desk in the same breath. That is not privacy — the cards are in every picture; what differs is which side of them each seat is shown.
